analysis: Examined ProviderLoop+Serve.swift (head) and ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift (patch plus base). Changed behavior in Serve.swift: (1) at shutdown, line 497 adds the selected-model recovery task (selectedModelRecovery.attempt?.task) to the preload task list, so it is cancelled and awaited via waitForPreloads before the inflight drain; (2) line 523 replaces the inline unload loop with unloadAllModelsForShutdown(), whose implementation is not in the supplied evidence. The removed loop waited for in-progress unloads and unloaded every slot; I could not confirm the new helper keeps the same semantics (wait for modelsUnloading, unload all slots), which matters for T-028 residual KV/GPU data and T-041 cache cleanup. StartupPreload patch (line ~304): finishStartupPreload now calls enqueueSelectedModelRecovery for memory-skipped, memory-failed and not-attempted candidates, guarded by !Task.isCancelled, !isShuttingDown and !startupPreloadStopRequested. It is not guarded by servingDrain.refusing, which the following updateAggregateCapacity check does use. Cannot verify whether enqueueSelectedModelRecovery or the recovery loop itself honors the add-on hold (TB-012/T-059, addonHoldActive/servingDrain.refusing) or service-change drain before loading a model. If it does not, a recovery load could occur beside add-on VMs or after a drain request. That implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery) is outside the supplied units, so this is an open integration question rather than a finding. Also unverified: recovery loads go through ensureModelLoaded with allowEviction false, and the hash/self-test paths apply. No change to the registration, attestation, key, encryption or App Attest authorization flow was observed in these units; the connection-control reader and the work FIFO are unchanged. No regressions are supported by the visible evidence.
